name: Sports, sponsorship and club or athlete-transfer laundering
description: Criminal funds are placed or integrated through professional sport by acquiring clubs, overpaying for sponsorship, naming rights or image rights, inflating player transfer fees, or paying agents and intermediaries commissions that have little to do with services. Valuations in sport are subjective and hard to benchmark, and ownership is often held through offshore vehicles, which gives illicit value a plausible commercial label. Betting-linked payments to players or officials add a match-fixing dimension.

sources.text: FATF, Money Laundering through the Football Sector, 2009
Council of Europe, Convention on the Manipulation of Sports Competitions (Macolin Convention), 2014
Europol, Money laundering in the sports sector (public threat material), various years

indicators.name: High-value asset held through opaque vehicle
indicators.canon: High-value asset held through opaque vehicle
indicators.desc: Property, art, vessels or other valuables are acquired or held via a company, trust or storage arrangement with concealed beneficial owners.
indicators.ctx: Club, stadium or franchise equity held through an offshore or opaque holding vehicle whose controller is not the stated investor.
indicators.fp: Privacy-motivated and estate-planning holdings can be lawful; verify beneficial ownership.

indicators.name: Beneficial owner or controller cannot be identified
indicators.canon: Beneficial owner or controller cannot be identified
indicators.desc: Ownership or governance is opaque and no natural person who owns or controls the entity can be identified after reasonable effort.
indicators.ctx: The person who really funds or controls the club or sponsoring company cannot be established after repeated enquiries, often after a quick succession of ownership changes.
indicators.fp: Complex but legitimate ownership may need extra time or documents to resolve.

indicators.name: Transaction price materially different from market value
indicators.canon: Transaction price materially different from market value
indicators.desc: Price paid differs sharply from market value, comparable sales or estimates without commercial justification.
indicators.ctx: Transfer fees, sponsorship deals or image-rights payments are well above or below what comparable players, clubs or audiences would command.
indicators.fp: Distressed sales, rare items, quality differences or volatile markets.

indicators.name: Fee arrangements disproportionate to services or paid by third parties
indicators.canon: Fee arrangements disproportionate to services or paid by third parties
indicators.ctx: Agent or intermediary commissions on transfers are large relative to the service, split across several parties, or paid by someone other than the club or player.

indicators.name: Circular or round-trip flows among related parties
indicators.canon: Circular or round-trip flows among related parties
indicators.desc: Funds or goods-linked payments loop back to the originator or between related counterparties, or are traded back and forth.
indicators.ctx: Sponsor money goes to a club, then returns to the sponsor's group through transfer fees, loans or related-party service contracts.
indicators.fp: Group treasury arrangements and legitimate back-to-back trading.

indicators.name: Players or officials receive payments from betting-linked parties
indicators.canon: Players or officials receive payments from betting-linked parties
indicators.desc: Payments to athletes, referees from unrelated parties.
indicators.ctx: Players, coaches or match officials receive payments from betting operators, bookmakers or associates of them.

indicators.name: Unusual betting patterns on lower-league or youth matches
indicators.canon: Unusual betting patterns on lower-league or youth matches
indicators.desc: Large late stakes on obscure markets.
indicators.ctx: Abnormal wagering on youth, lower-league or friendly fixtures linked to accounts connected to club insiders or investors.

indicators.name: Secrecy or low-transparency jurisdiction nexus
indicators.desc: Entities, accounts or assets are booked in jurisdictions offering strong secrecy or limited transparency, including where unrelated to the entity's operations.
indicators.ctx: Funding for the club, sponsor or transfer comes from a secrecy jurisdiction with no link to the club, league or sponsor's business.
indicators.fp: Legitimate holding structures and funds use such jurisdictions for tax neutrality or legal reasons.

indicators.name: Image-rights or endorsement income paid to a third-country entity instead of the athlete
indicators.canon: Image-rights or endorsement income paid to a third-country entity instead of the athlete
indicators.desc: Earnings from endorsement, image or commercial rights are directed to a company or account in a jurisdiction unconnected to the athlete or the paying party, with no clear contractual basis.
indicators.ctx: Image-rights fees for a player are paid to an offshore company owned by a nominee or an agent, not the player.
indicators.fp: Athletes legitimately use personal service companies and image-rights vehicles, often for tax planning. Concern arises when the vehicle's location, ownership or timing has no commercial explanation.

indicators.name: Sponsorship or naming-rights spend with no measurable promotional deliverables
indicators.canon: Sponsorship or naming-rights spend with no measurable promotional deliverables
indicators.desc: A sponsor pays substantial amounts to a sports body, club or event but there is little evidence of advertising, activation or audience reach, or the sponsor has no relevant business.
indicators.ctx: A newly formed company with no marketing history pays an unusually high sponsorship fee that cannot be tied to audience or exposure.
indicators.fp: Philanthropic or owner-affiliated sponsorships and early-stage brand investment may have little measurable return.
